narrative: OMX30 faces significant headwinds this morning following a severe US tech rout (NASDAQ -4.25%) and sharp VIX spike to 33.21, signaling broad risk-off positioning. Swedish equities are caught between deteriorating US sentiment and domestic technical weakness: Stochastic K at 11.7 (deeply oversold) and RSI at 38.26 signal mean reversion risk, while the index trades -2.4% below its 50-MA and MACD has rolled negative. However, the index remains +0.4% above the 200-MA (bull market support), and the DAX/CAC show more resilience than US peers, suggesting European valuation attraction may cushion the decline. The correlation signal of -0.821% reflects genuine risk-off, but oversold technicals create tactical bounce potential intraday. Yield compression (-1.94% on US 10Y) will pressure Swedish banks despite wider NIM mechanics, as risk appetite dominance matters more than carry signals in this environment.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens to significant selling pressure—expect -1% to -1.5% gap down at open tracking US tech contagion (NASDAQ -4.25%) and VIX surge. Key support: 3085 (lower Bollinger band); 3050 (psychological level). Resistance: 3123 (yesterday close), 3155 (50-MA). Watch for bounce attempts if Stochastic K overshoots below 10—mean reversion traders may step in mid-morning. Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A) will trade weaker despite yield mechanics due to risk-off rotation, though AstraZeneca and Essity should outperform as defensive havens. Industrials/Exporters (Volvo B, Atlas Copco A, Ericsson B) face dual headwinds: US sentiment contagion + no USD/SEK relief (USD/SEK flat). Watch for US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET—any softness could trigger further liquidation. Volume and breadth critical; monitor if decline holds above 3050 or breaks lower.
